(2024). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
description: MMMU is a massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark of 11.5K college-level questions collected from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks. It covers 6 disciplines, 30 subjects, 183 subfields, and 30 heterogeneous image types to evaluate expert-level perception, knowledge, and reasoning.
name: MMMU
publisher: University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, IN.AI Research
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors and subjects, served as annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control included lexical overlap and source URL similarity to identify potential duplicates, author review to remove duplicates, distribution of problems among co-authors for format and typo checking, categorization into four difficulty levels, exclusion of about 10% of very easy problems, secondary review-team vetting, and regular audits of random samples.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, collected questions and annotated fields including question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation if available. They were instructed that all questions must contain one or more images, be written in English, meet college-level difficulty, be unambiguous, and adhere to copyright and licensing regulations; questions with easily accessible answers were discouraged to reduce data contamination.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the manual curation process may carry biases. It also describes design decisions to reduce bias and contamination: selecting diverse sources rather than a single source, avoiding questions with immediately available answers, and instructing annotators to adhere to copyright and licensing regulations.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was collected in three stages: selecting subjects based on the prevalence of useful visual inputs, recruiting over 50 university students including co-authors as annotators, and collecting multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, quizzes, and lecture materials, with new questions created based on annotator expertise when necessary.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data consisted of college-level multimodal questions from free online resources, textbooks, quizzes, lecture materials, and other study materials, including images such as diagrams, charts, photographs, tables, music sheets, chemical structures, and medical images.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' and college exams are not the only tasks an AGI should tackle. It also notes that the manual curation process may carry biases and that the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels—very easy, easy, medium, and hard—and approximately 10% classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark. The final dataset was split into a few-shot development set, validation set, and test set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent data cleaning by detecting suspected duplicates using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, manual author review to eliminate duplicates, format and typo checking, standardization into a structured JSON format with image file references interleaved in questions/options/explanations, and filtering out approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The appendix includes a version change log documenting updates from V1 to V4, including changes on Nov. 27, Dec. 18, Dec. 21, and June 13.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the benchmark as important for monitoring progress toward Expert AGI because such systems could substitute for skilled human labor and create risks of job displacement and economic disruption. It also discusses ethical considerations including copyright, licensing compliance, privacy-law compliance, and avoiding collection of private information.
rai:dataUseCases: MMMU is intended to evaluate large multimodal models on expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning across disciplines, monitor progress toward Expert AGI, benchmark multimodal foundation models, support hyperparameter selection via its validation set, and stimulate development of next-generation multimodal foundation models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicate problems; a user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The protocol instructs annotators to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
